transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I conducted your post-cataract surgery follow-up check and I'm here to answer any questions you may have about your recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, thank you for checking in. Yes, I do have some questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can start light gardening, like watering plants or gentle weeding, after about 1 week after surgery. Just be careful not to get any dirt or debris in your eyes. And remember to wear your sunglasses when you're outside.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You should start using the preservative-free eye drops for dry eyes four times a day, as soon as you can after surgery. If you were already using eye drops before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's normal for your eyes to be sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and you just feel like things are brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside should help. However, if you're experiencing significant pain or discomfort, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess it further. 

Do you have any other questions?
